screening_decisions.reason: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not an RCT. The selection criteria require RCTs only.
This is a symposium/educational article discussing various OHSS prevention methods, not an RCT.
This is an RCT comparing two different timing strategies for cabergoline (dopamine agonist) administration for OHSS prevention in IVF patients.
This is an RCT comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) alone vs coasting alone vs combined intervention for OHSS prevention in IVF/ICSI patients.
This is a case report describing one patient treated with high dose cabergoline, not an RCT.
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing cabergoline vs placebo for OHSS prevention in IVF patients.
This is an observational study about cardiac valve regurgitation in Parkinson's disease patients, not about OHSS prevention in ART.
This is an animal study in rats investigating VEGF mechanisms, not an RCT in humans for OHSS prevention in ART.
This is a Cochrane review about GnRH antagonists, not dopamine agonists. Also not an RCT.
This is a cross-sectional study about cardiac valvular abnormalities in hyperprolactinemia patients, not about OHSS prevention in ART.
This is a retrospective case-control study comparing IVM vs IVF, not an RCT. Also does not involve dopamine agonists.
This is a systematic review and network meta-analysis, not an RCT. The selection criteria require RCTs only.
This is a case report about two patients with gonadotropin-producing pituitary adenomas, not an RCT.
This is a clinical trial of SU5416 (VEGF inhibitor) in cancer patients, not about dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention in ART.
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing quinagolide (dopamine agonist) vs placebo for OHSS prevention in IVF patients.
This is a prospective randomized study comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) vs no medication for OHSS prevention in ART patients.
This is a review article analyzing efficacy of dopamine agonists, not an RCT.
This is a review article about different IVF methods, not an RCT and not about dopamine agonists.
This is primarily an animal study in rats investigating cabergoline mechanisms. While it mentions some human oocyte donor data, it is not an RCT.
This is a case report about a patient with gonadotroph adenoma, not an RCT.
This RCT compares IVF vs ICSI fertilization techniques in IVM cycles, not dopamine agonists. The intervention does not match the review question.
RCT comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) vs no treatment in women at high risk for OHSS undergoing IVF/ICSI. Primary outcome was OHSS incidence. Meets all selection criteria.
Abstract describes a meta-analysis about bacterial vaginosis in IVF patients, not an RCT about dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention. Mismatched content and wrong study design.
Cochrane review about volume expanders, not an RCT. Does not evaluate dopamine agonists.
RCT comparing cabergoline (dopamine agonist) vs intravenous albumin in high-risk women for OHSS. Outcomes include moderate/severe OHSS. Meets selection criteria.
Systematic review and meta-analysis, not an RCT. Wrong study design per selection criteria.
Review/guideline document, not an RCT. Wrong study design.

RCT comparing cabergoline + GnRH antagonist rescue vs cabergoline alone in high-risk OHSS patients. Both groups receive dopamine agonist; tests additional intervention. Outcomes include moderate/severe OHSS. Meets criteria.
Review article about dopamine agonists for hyperprolactinaemia, not OHSS prevention. Not an RCT. Wrong topic and study design.
Brief commentary/statement about OHSS etiology, not an RCT. Wrong study design.
Literature review discussing pathophysiology. Mentions a trial but is itself a review, not an RCT. Wrong study design.
Commentary/review about GnRH agonist triggering mechanism, not an RCT. Wrong study design.
Prospective, randomized, double-blind RCT comparing cabergoline vs placebo in oocyte donors at risk of OHSS. Outcomes include moderate OHSS incidence. Meets all selection criteria.
Nested case-control study about cardiovascular safety in Parkinson's/hyperprolactinaemia patients, not an RCT for OHSS prevention. Wrong study design and population.
Non-randomized clinical trial with historical controls. Selection criteria require RCTs only. Wrong study design.
Case series (4 patients) describing treatment of established OHSS, not prevention. Not an RCT. Wrong study design and focus.
Symposium presentation/abstract, not an RCT. Wrong study design.
Randomized comparative study comparing calcium gluconate vs cabergoline (dopamine agonist) in high-risk OHSS patients. Outcomes include OHSS occurrence. Meets selection criteria.
Cochrane review protocol (Spanish language). Not an RCT. Wrong study design.
Prospective cohort study, not randomized. Focuses on follicular fluid hormone levels rather than primary outcomes (OHSS incidence, live birth). Wrong study design.
This study is about cancer treatment using VEGF blocking therapy, not about dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention in ART. Wrong population and intervention.
This is a review article summarizing classifications and preventive measures for OHSS, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a cross-sectional study about dopamine agonists for prolactinoma treatment, not for OHSS prevention. Wrong population and outcome.
This is a review article about cabergoline for OHSS, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is about PCOS treatment update, not specifically about dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention. Wrong intervention focus.
This is a review article about ART complications including OHSS, not an RCT about dopamine agonists. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is an RCT comparing albumin vs cabergoline (dopamine agonist) for OHSS prevention in high-risk IVF patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is described as a prospective controlled study, not explicitly an RCT. The study design does not clearly meet the RCT requirement.
This is a Cochrane review about coasting for OHSS prevention, not an RCT about dopamine agonists. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a Cochrane review about metformin for PCOS in IVF, not about dopamine agonists. Wrong intervention.
This is a systematic review about coasting, not an RCT about dopamine agonists. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a Cochrane review about luteal phase support, not about dopamine agonists for OHSS prevention. Wrong intervention.
This is an animal study in rodents, not a human RCT. Does not meet population or study design criteria.

This is an RCT comparing bromocriptine (dopamine agonist) vs folic acid (placebo) for OHSS prevention in IVF patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.
This is described as a retrospective study, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a randomized study comparing HES alone vs HES + cabergoline (dopamine agonist) for OHSS prevention in IVF patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.
This is a prospective study comparing bromocriptine to historical controls, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a review article about OHSS prevention strategies, not an RCT about dopamine agonists. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is described as a retrospective study, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.

This study is a clinical trial comparing cabergoline (a dopamine agonist) versus coasting (another intervention) for preventing OHSS in high-risk ART patients. The study design appears to be an RCT comparing a dopamine agonist with another intervention for OHSS prevention in ART, which meets the selection criteria. The abstract mentions 60 women in ART cycles at risk of OHSS, and the intervention is cabergoline, a selective D2 dopamine receptor agonist.

This is a basic science study in rodents (CD1 mice) investigating the VEGF/VEGFR-2 pathway in corpora lutea during pregnancy. It is not an RCT, does not involve dopamine agonists, and does not address OHSS prevention in ART. The study focuses on embryonic development and luteal function in mice, which is outside the scope of the systematic review.

This is explicitly described as a randomized controlled study evaluating cabergoline (0.25mg dopamine agonist) versus no treatment for preventing OHSS in women at high risk undergoing IVF/ICSI treatment cycles. The study included 200 women and reported significantly reduced OHSS incidence in the cabergoline group. This clearly meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.

This is a prospective randomized controlled trial investigating cabergoline (a dopamine agonist) versus no medication for reducing OHSS in high-risk women undergoing ART. The study enrolled 40 infertile women at risk of OHSS and found significantly lower ascites and moderate OHSS incidence in the cabergoline group. This meets all selection criteria: RCT design, dopamine agonist intervention, OHSS prevention in ART.

This study investigates valvular heart disease in patients taking dopamine agonists for Parkinson's disease treatment. While it involves dopamine agonists (pergolide, cabergoline), the population is Parkinson's disease patients, not women undergoing ART. The study does not address OHSS prevention in ART and is therefore outside the scope of this systematic review.

This is a review article providing an update on OHSS, not a primary research study. The selection criteria specifically require RCTs, and review articles do not meet this criterion. While the topic is relevant to OHSS, the study design does not qualify for inclusion in this systematic review.
